key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports welding process maps that distinguish defective from defect-free operating windows while reducing force fluctuations and thermal gradients.
method: Simulate temperature, axial force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Evaluate rotational speed, welding speed and bottom preheating against experimental results.
evidence_signal: The ANNs achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99; 60 °C bottom preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N and raised peak temperature from 70 °C to about 100 °C.
watch_item: Prediction accuracy and optimal settings are established only within the tested parameter space; transfer to other materials or welding configurations requires validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
